articles.title: Show Live Crypto Prices in a Laravel App Without Float Bugs
articles.excerpt: A price widget in a Laravel app looks like a ten minute job: call an API, cache the result, print the number. The two places it goes wrong are the cache (you hammer the API on every page view) and the…
articles.body: A price widget in a Laravel app looks like a ten minute job: call an API, cache the result, print the number. The two places it goes wrong are the cache (you hammer the API on every page view) and the math (you cast a price to float and lose digits). This post wires up both properly, using the official PHP SDK for the Bitculator Data API. 1. Install the SDK composer require bitculator/sdk The SDK needs PHP 8.1+, ext-curl and ext-json , and has no other dependencies. Get an API key from your Bitculator developer page and put it in .env : BITCULATOR_API_KEY = your-key-here Keep the key server-side. It is a Bearer token and does not belong in JavaScript. 2.

articles.title: Building Algerian Darija TTS: LoRA, Code-Switching, and Natiq-dz-ARG
articles.excerpt: Disclosure: I'm sharing this project from Natiq Studio, the team developing Natiq-dz-ARG. Text-to-speech models can produce impressive English, French, and Modern Standard Arabic. Algerian Darija intr…
articles.body: Disclosure: I'm sharing this project from Natiq Studio, the team developing Natiq-dz-ARG. Text-to-speech models can produce impressive English, French, and Modern Standard Arabic. Algerian Darija introduces a different challenge: the same sentence can move between Arabic and French while retaining a distinctly Algerian rhythm. At Natiq Studio , we've been working on that problem with Natiq-dz-ARG , an open-weight speech model adapted specifically for Algerian Darija. This article covers the main engineering lessons behind it and where developers can experiment with the release. Why code-switching matters Consider this everyday sentence: سلام خويا، حبيت نسقسيك على la livraison تاع هاد produit.

articles.title: One CLI, Two Identities: MCP Client and MCP Server
articles.excerpt: MCP (Model Context Protocol) has become the de facto standard for AI tool interconnection — the community hosts 5800+ MCP servers you can plug into. Most tools pick one side: they either consume MCP s…
articles.body: MCP (Model Context Protocol) has become the de facto standard for AI tool interconnection — the community hosts 5800+ MCP servers you can plug into. Most tools pick one side: they either consume MCP servers or provide tools as one. hmharness — an open-source (MIT) agent framework for HarmonyOS/OpenHarmony development — took the uncommon "both directions" approach. Identity 1: Client (borrowing the ecosystem) hmharness connects to all 5800+ community MCP servers over both stdio and HTTP transports. When its agent works on a task, it can call any capability the ecosystem already has — query databases, read web pages, operate SaaS tools — without implementing each one itself. Stand on the ecosystem, don't rebuild it.

articles.title: Variational Inference: Why the ELBO Trades Accuracy for Tractability
articles.excerpt: Variational Inference: Why the ELBO Trades Accuracy for Tractability Bayesian inference is easy to write down and hard to compute. Given data x and latent variables z , Bayes' rule gives the posterior…
articles.body: Variational Inference: Why the ELBO Trades Accuracy for Tractability Bayesian inference is easy to write down and hard to compute. Given data x and latent variables z , Bayes' rule gives the posterior: p ( z ∣ x ) = p ( x ) p ( x ∣ z ) p ( z ) ​ The numerator is usually easy: a prior p ( z ) and a likelihood p ( x ∣ z ) . The denominator, the evidence p ( x ) , is the problem. It is an integral over every possible value of z : p ( x ) = ∫ p ( x ∣ z ) p ( z ) d z For any realistic model, that integral has no closed form and is too high-dimensional to compute numerically. Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) attacks the problem by sampling, and given enough time it can be asymptotically exact.

articles.body: Routing a support ticket requires a destination your application can use. Jev accepts context and questions with predefined answer spaces, then returns structured decisions and probabilities. That makes it relevant wherever software needs a bounded judgment, such as choosing a queue, assessing relevance, or scoring against a rubric. The engineering challenge is deciding when those outputs are reliable enough to trigger an action. What Jev is, and when it appeared TypeSafe AI introduced Jev in early access on September 15, 2026, describing it as its first "System One" model. The category name draws on the distinction between fast, intuitive judgment and slower, deliberate reasoning. It is TypeSafe's terminology for its approach.

articles.excerpt: If you run a small business and you are choosing an AI assistant, "which one is best?" is the wrong first question. A better one: which tools are people actually using, and which way is that moving? I…
articles.body: If you run a small business and you are choosing an AI assistant, "which one is best?" is the wrong first question. A better one: which tools are people actually using, and which way is that moving? I track public data on this. It is not a count of users, and it is not a quality ranking. It is the share of website visits that arrive from each AI chatbot, measured by StatCounter on sites that use it. That shows which assistants send people out to the web. September 2026: share of AI-chatbot referrals ChatGPT: 80.5% Gemini: 10.9% (up 3.0 points over three months) Perplexity: 5.8% (down 2.0 points) Microsoft Copilot: 1.8% (down 1.7 points) Claude: 1.0% (down 2.8 points) Three things stand out ChatGPT is far ahead, but Gemini is the only major tool gaining share in this data.

articles.title: Give Claude and Cursor your bookmarks: the Kyurations MCP server
articles.excerpt: Most of us save a lot of links. For years, our AI tools could not see any of them. When you ask Claude about something you read, it answers from the open web, not from the sources you picked. So we ad…
articles.body: Most of us save a lot of links. For years, our AI tools could not see any of them. When you ask Claude about something you read, it answers from the open web, not from the sources you picked. So we added a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server to Kyurations, our bookmarking app. This post explains what the server does, how to connect it, and what you can ask it. What the server does Kyurations speaks MCP. That means Claude, Cursor and any agent that talks the protocol can search, read and help organise the library you have curated. The endpoint is: https://www.kyurations.in/api/mcp The tools are in two groups. Read tools. These never leave your library. Search the library. Semantic and keyword search across everything you saved. Every result comes back with its link. Filter by facet.

articles.title: Satellites watch an escaping Antarctic iceberg | Space photo of the day for Oct. 28, 2026
articles.excerpt: Iceberg A-81 escaping the Weddell Sea and drifting near the edge of South Georgia's underwater shelf.
articles.body: Iceberg A-81 escaping the Weddell Sea and drifting near the edge of South Georgia's underwater shelf. The image was captured on Oct. 20, 2026. (Image credit: NASA Earth Observatory/Michala Garrison) An iceberg has quickly escaped from the Weddell Sea in Antarctica, on its way to an icy new destination. What is it? As captured by a satellite in orbit, the Antarctic iceberg A-81 has quite quickly (for an iceberg) parted ways from its icy home, breaking off to drift toward a shallow underwater shelf in Georgia. The 600-square-mile (1,550-square-kilometer) iceberg first broke off from the Brunt Ice Shelf in January of 2023. Now, generally speaking, giant icebergs don't travel that fast.

articles.title: Astronomers found a mysterious object beyond Neptune, and it could be a new dwarf planet
articles.excerpt: The Vera Rubin Observatory has discovered a suspected dwarf planet beyond Neptune's orbit. If confirmed, it would be the sixth known dwarf planet in our solar system.
articles.body: The powerful Vera Rubin Observatory has spotted what seems to be a dwarf planet circling the sun in the frigid depths beyond Neptune. The icy object, known as 2026 ED138, is likely between 600 and 1500 kilometers (373 to 972 miles) wide, scientists say. It's therefore probably big enough to be sculpted into a sphere by its own gravity — a key characteristic that separates dwarf planets from asteroids and other small space rocks. And if 2026 ED138 is indeed a dwarf planet, that's a pretty big deal, as astronomers have confirmed just five of them to date: Pluto , Ceres, Eris, Haumea and Makemake . An illustration of the solar system showing the orbital pathway of newly discovered dwarf planet candidate 2026 ED138 (ED138). (Image credit: NSF–DOE Vera C. Rubin Observatory/NOIRLab/SLAC/AURA/R.

articles.body: Space tourists and citizen astronauts rejoice! A new suborbital spacecraft is about to be introduced that will fly ticketholders on brief, suborbital journeys just above Earth. Virgin Galactic plans to unveil its first Delta-class spaceship on Wednesday (Oct. 28), before transporting the spacecraft from Mesa, Arizona, to Spaceport America in New Mexico. Alongside that reveal, the company will also announce the spacecraft's name, selected through a public vote held across more than 80 countries. Following its debut, the Delta-class vehicle will journey to the spaceport attached to Virgin Galactic's VMS Eve carrier aircraft, marking a transition from assembly to the beginning of official flight testing.

articles.title: Black holes can split in two — but only if they spin at extreme speeds
articles.excerpt: Scientists have long known that when two black holes collide, they merge to create a more massive black hole. New research suggests that the opposite may happen too: single black holes may split in tw…
articles.body: Scientists have long known that when two black holes collide, they merge to create a more massive black hole. These events are so violent that they set the very fabric of space ringing with ripples called gravitational waves. Now, new research suggests that the opposite may happen, too: single black holes may be able to split in two. But this can only happen if that progenitor black hole is spinning at maximum possible speed. That speed prevents the black holes from immediately falling back on each other. There are physical laws in place that would usually prevent black holes from splitting in two; the team behind this research investigated whether there are conditions in which these laws can be temporarily bypassed.
